bugs: Order::markAsPaid (app/Models/Order.php:43) checks the in-memory status, not the DB state, and takes no lock. Probe: two stale instances of the same order each dispatched a job (2 pushed).

Two copies of the job can run at once: there is no WithoutOverlapping or ShouldBeUnique, so both see shipment_reference null and POST. A duplicate shipment is prevented only if the partner honours the Idempotency-Key header (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:51,77).
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:22 — the class-level explanatory comment mixes the rationale for retryUntil and MaxExceptions; it is acceptable but borderline.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:128-134 — the try/catch that rolls back shipment_notified_at is extra ceremony; it is correct but heavy.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:51-55 — a nested if could be collapsed into one condition.
tests/Feature/OrderShipmentTest.php:108-117 — the mail-failure test resets the container with forgetInstance and clearResolvedInstances, which is brittle.
strengths: The most modern conventions: backed enums with casts, #[Fillable], and the queue attributes #[Timeout], #[Backoff], #[MaxExceptions] and #[DeleteWhenMissingModels] on Laravel 13.
Honours Retry-After on 429 via release(), and uses a time-bounded retryUntil so rate-limit releases don't exhaust tries.
The job guards against trashed and non-paid orders. A probe confirmed a cancelled order on a real database queue is not shipped and does not fail.
An atomic conditional-update claim guarantees the email goes out once, even when retried after a mail failure.
Account-wide RateLimited middleware, verified by a probe (the 6th job was released).
failed() records the reason and leaves an existing shipment alone. A 422 is surfaced without retrying.
Broad Pest tests covering 422, 429 with and without Retry-After, 5xx, hangs, a missing id, recovery, and dispatch after commit.

bugs: A 429 is treated as a generic exception via $response->throw() (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:105). It ignores Retry-After and uses up the MaxExceptions(8) budget during rate-limit storms instead of releasing.
The job does not check that the order is paid. Probe: dispatching it for an unpaid order created a shipment.
markAsPaid has the same stale-instance race as impl-1 (app/Models/Order.php:42), with no DB-level claim. WithoutOverlapping plus refresh() does mitigate a duplicate shipment.
antipatterns: tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php was deleted from the base app, which is outside the task's scope.
app/Models/Order.php:35 — shipment_notified_at is cast but is not in Fillable or the task's column list; it is an implicit extra column with no factory state.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:58-64 — checks shipment_status twice; the flow would read more clearly with createShipment returning a bool.
tests/Feature/SendOrderToWarehouseTest.php:193-203 — mocks the Mail facade and then re-fakes it; this container juggling is brittle.
strengths: A 422 goes through $this->fail(), so the reason lands both on the order and in failed_jobs. A probe on a real database queue confirmed status failed, the reason recorded, and no retry.
refresh() at the start of handle, together with per-order WithoutOverlapping, stops concurrent duplicate shipments.
failed() uses withTrashed->find and skips orders already Sent.
Modern queue attributes, enums and Http::baseUrl.
Concise tests using a dataset across 429 and 5xx statuses, plus a check of the configurable URL.

bugs: markAsPaid uses withTrashed() (app/Models/Order.php:54), so a cancelled (soft-deleted) pending order gets marked paid and a job is dispatched. The job then no-ops, so nothing ships, but the state is odd.

notifyCustomer sends before recording shipment_notified_at (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:145-147), so a crash between the two could send the email twice. WithoutOverlapping keeps the window small.
antipatterns: app/Models/Order.php:19-27 — string class constants instead of backed enums with casts, which is not modern Laravel.

app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:7-22 — the legacy Dispatchable, InteractsWithQueue, Queueable and SerializesModels traits instead of Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable; properties instead of queue attributes.
app/Models/Order.php:13 — #[UseFactory] is redundant alongside the conventional HasFactory resolution.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:26,29-34,60 and app/Models/Order.php:47-50 — comment density is higher than the rest of the codebase, and some comments narrate what the code does.
.env.example was edited, which is fine, but the AppServiceProvider imports the job just for a RATE_LIMITER constant — extra coupling.
strengths: markAsPaid claims the order atomically with a conditional update. A probe confirmed two stale instances queue only one job, and a rollback test proves dispatch waits for the commit.

handle reloads through the default soft-delete scope (find returns null when the order is cancelled) and requires paid status. A probe confirmed a cancelled order on a real database queue is not shipped and does not fail.

The fullest error classification: 2xx with a missing id is a permanent failure (avoids duplicate shipments); 429 is released honouring a capped Retry-After; 5xx and 408 throw for backoff; other 4xx such as 422 and 401 are surfaced to ops.
recordFailure is scoped to whereNull(shipment_reference) and the soft-delete scope, so it never overwrites a sent shipment or touches a cancelled order.
Per-order WithoutOverlapping plus account-wide RateLimited. The rate-limit behaviour is tested end to end with freezeTime and travel, and Http::preventStrayRequests is set globally in Pest.php.
The richest Pest suite: describe blocks, an after-commit rollback test, mail-failure recovery, a cancelled order on failure, and a 401.

v.rationale: All three suites pass and share the same backbone: dispatch after commit, an account-wide RateLimited('warehouse') at 5 per second, a time-bounded retryUntil with maxExceptions, a guard against cancelled orders, a single customer email, and failed() recording the reason. Correctness on the focus area decides the ranking. impl-3 is the only one whose markAsPaid is race-safe (a conditional update; a probe confirmed one job from two stale instances). It also reloads the order with the soft-delete scope and checks paid status, classifies 2xx-without-id, 429, 5xx/408 and other 4xx correctly, and has the most behavioural tests (a real rollback test, the rate limit end to end). It loses points for legacy job traits, string constants instead of enums, and comment noise. impl-1 is the most idiomatic and modern, and honours Retry-After and paid status. However, its markAsPaid can dispatch twice from stale instances (probe-confirmed) and the job has no overlap protection, so concurrent runs could create duplicate shipments unless the partner honours the Idempotency-Key. impl-2 is equally modern and does stop concurrent duplicates with WithoutOverlapping and refresh. But it treats 429 as a generic exception (ignoring Retry-After and burning the exception budget), ships unpaid orders if the job is dispatched for one (probe-confirmed), deleted the base ExampleTest, and has the thinnest tests.
